learning_takeaway.selected: Represent connections by vertices and edges, then use structural constraints such as bipartite colorability.
learning_takeaway.actual: Separate a network’s underlying connections from the way its vertices and edges are drawn or labeled.

learning_takeaway.selected: Append committed changes separately before transferring them into the main database, allowing concurrent readers.
learning_takeaway.actual: See how SQLite's WAL mode appends changes separately before checkpointing them into the main database, allowing concurrent readers.

learning_takeaway.selected: Move committed log content into the database as a separate operation from reading, writing, and committing.
learning_takeaway.actual: In SQLite, move committed log content into the database as a separate operation from reading, writing, and committing.

learning_takeaway.selected: Use a one-position contrast between otherwise matching words as evidence that two sounds distinguish meanings.
learning_takeaway.actual: Use a spoken-language word pair differing in one sound as evidence of contrastive phonemes, without treating failure to find a pair as proof of equivalence.

learning_takeaway.selected: Akbar tied administrators’ rank and cavalry responsibilities to reassigned revenue allocations, limiting independent hereditary power.
learning_takeaway.actual: Under Akbar, administrators’ ranks combined civil service and cavalry responsibilities with revenue allocations that could be reassigned.

learning_takeaway.selected: An uprising against plantation slavery developed into independence, while foreign governments’ recognition remained constrained by their own slaveholding interests.
learning_takeaway.actual: An uprising against plantation slavery led to independence, while U.S. policy and delayed recognition reflected shifting concerns about slavery, trade and diplomacy.

learning_takeaway.selected: Success in literary and Confucian examinations became a route into government, although most candidates never obtained office.
learning_takeaway.actual: In the Song case, literary and Confucian examinations offered a route into government, but most candidates never became officials.

learning_takeaway.selected: A reachable area follows paths and travel costs in a network, so it differs from a circle drawn at a fixed distance.
learning_takeaway.actual: A reachable area follows network paths and travel costs, so it need not match a circle drawn at a fixed distance.

learning_takeaway.selected: Offerings, images and acts of hospitality create a ritual encounter with a deity; the details vary among Hindu communities.
learning_takeaway.actual: Offerings and visual interaction with deity images are common elements of Hindu puja; practices vary with the deity and community.

learning_takeaway.selected: Food or other offerings made to a deity can be shared with worshippers, connecting divine hospitality with communal receipt.
learning_takeaway.actual: Offerings made to a deity can later be shared among worshippers, connecting devotion with communal distribution.

learning_takeaway.selected: Jewish ritual bathing can shape substantial communal architecture, as Cologne’s medieval bath descends deep enough to reach groundwater.
learning_takeaway.actual: A Jewish ritual bath can be studied through its built setting; Cologne’s medieval mikveh reaches groundwater deep beneath the former Jewish quarter.

learning_takeaway.selected: A portable shrine amulet is selected for a particular request and carried as an expression of a kami’s protection.
learning_takeaway.actual: A portable shrine amulet is often selected for a particular request and carried as an expression of a kami’s protection.

learning_takeaway.selected: A narrative can reveal information beyond its established focalization norm, making an exceptional disclosure meaningful.
learning_takeaway.actual: A narrative can reveal information beyond its established focalization norm; identifying this excess depends on the particular text.

learning_takeaway.selected: Repeating initial words across phrases or lines builds rhythmic and emotional accumulation.
learning_takeaway.actual: Repeating initial words across phrases or lines can build rhythmic and emotional accumulation.

learning_takeaway.selected: Thoreau’s account of life by Walden Pond makes withdrawal from conventional society a literary experiment in how to live.
learning_takeaway.actual: Thoreau’s account of life by Walden Pond invites an editorial reading of withdrawal from conventional society as an experiment in ways of living.

learning_takeaway.selected: Pound uses a troubadour-warrior’s voice and recurring end-words to intensify a dramatic monologue praising combat.
learning_takeaway.actual: Pound adopts a troubadour-warrior’s voice and recurring end-words; an editorial reading hears their repetition intensifying the monologue’s praise of combat.

learning_takeaway.selected: Williams’s short lines split ordinary compound words, making the placement of everyday objects inseparable from the poem’s pacing.
learning_takeaway.actual: Williams splits compound words across short lines; an editorial reading interprets that lineation as shaping pacing and attention.

learning_takeaway.selected: Brooks places the repeated group pronoun at line endings, joining collective self-assertion to a rhythm that stops with mortality.
learning_takeaway.actual: Brooks places a collective pronoun at line endings; an editorial reading connects the recurring group voice with the poem’s final reference to death.

learning_takeaway.selected: Ali advocated English ghazals that retain autonomous couplets and shared rhyme-refrain patterns instead of merely borrowing the name.
learning_takeaway.actual: Ali promoted the traditional ghazal in English through poetry and anthology editorship, emphasizing the autonomy of its couplets.

learning_takeaway.selected: Bishop’s villanelle expands from minor misplaced objects to personal loss, making its repeated assurance increasingly difficult for the speaker to sustain.
learning_takeaway.actual: Bishop’s villanelle moves from small losses toward personal loss; an editorial reading hears increasing strain in its repeated assurance.

learning_takeaway.selected: A water-soluble sugar drawing beneath a varnish ground lifts away in water, exposing drawn areas for subsequent aquatint and etching.
learning_takeaway.actual: A water-soluble sugar drawing beneath a varnish ground lifts away in water, exposing drawn areas for etching, often after aquatint.

learning_takeaway.selected: A drawn, painted or scratched glass plate becomes a negative when placed over light-sensitive paper and exposed to light.
learning_takeaway.actual: A drawn, painted or scratched glass plate acts as a negative for exposing light-sensitive paper.

learning_takeaway.selected: Objects laid on photosensitive paper control exposure directly: opaque areas stay light, while translucent objects produce intermediate tones.
learning_takeaway.actual: In the described paper process, opaque objects leave light areas while translucent objects can yield intermediate tones during direct exposure.

learning_takeaway.selected: Fresco a secco applies paint to a dry wall surface, distinguishing it from wet-plaster buon fresco.
learning_takeaway.actual: Fresco a secco applies paint to a dry plaster surface, contrasting with buon fresco on wet plaster.

learning_takeaway.selected: A fresco painter lays only the area of fresh finishing plaster that can be painted that day, dividing the work into daily sections.
learning_takeaway.actual: A fresco painter prepares fresh finishing plaster in daily working sections sized to what can be painted while the surface remains workable.

learning_takeaway.selected: Unmarked areas around or within depicted forms can actively describe an object, as blank chair shapes do among the marks in Asawa’s drawing.
learning_takeaway.actual: Unmarked areas around or within depicted forms can describe an object, as blank chair shapes do in Ruth Asawa’s 1965 lithograph Chair (TAM.1558-II).

learning_takeaway.selected: Asawa’s drawing lets chairs emerge both from dense marker patterns and from unmarked gaps, making absence as constructive as the surrounding marks.
learning_takeaway.actual: In the 1965 lithograph Chair (TAM.1558-II), patterned marks and unmarked spaces both delineate chairs, making negative space an active part of the composition.

learning_takeaway.selected: Morris’s textile design uses indigo-discharge printing to give fruit-stealing thrushes and foliage crisp detail within a repeated pattern.
learning_takeaway.actual: Morris used indigo-discharge printing for Strawberry Thief, a textile pattern inspired by fruit-stealing thrushes in his garden.

learning_takeaway.selected: Morris’s Wandle design uses a notably large pattern repeat, making the scale of repetition a defining feature of its textile composition.
learning_takeaway.actual: Wandle’s repeat measures 98.4 by 44.5 centimeters; the V&A identifies it as the largest Morris attempted.

learning_takeaway.selected: The so-called tapestry is wool embroidery on joined linen panels; its stitching carries a continuous historical narrative rather than a woven pictorial structure.
learning_takeaway.actual: The Bayeux Tapestry’s narrative is embroidered in wool on joined linen panels rather than woven as a pictorial tapestry.

learning_takeaway.selected: Hokusai frames a small Mount Fuji inside the threatening wave and uses blue pigments to bind this striking contrast of scale into the print.
learning_takeaway.actual: Hokusai uses perspective and framing to make Mount Fuji appear as a small triangular form within the much larger wave.
